content.text: Let me restructure with a robust shell launcher that locates Python even with an unusual PATH:

arguments.command:
cd /app/submit && cp run solver.py && cat > run << 'SHEOF'
#!/bin/sh
# Launcher for the IPv6 lookup pipeline compiler/lookup service.
#
# Locates a Python 3 interpreter (preferring PATH, then the usual absolute
# locations so that this also works with an empty or minimal PATH) and execs
# the solver.  The solver may build core.c into a shared object on first use;
# when no C compiler is available it falls back to an equivalent pure-Python
# implementation of the optimizer.

self=$0
case "$self" in
  */*) DIR=${self%/*} ;;
  *) DIR=. ;;
esac

if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  exec python3 "$DIR/solver.py" "$@"
fi
for c in /usr/bin/python3 /usr/local/bin/python3 /bin/python3 \
         /usr/bin/python3.11 /usr/local/bin/python3.11 /opt/python3/bin/python3; do
  if [ -x "$c" ]; then
    exec "$c" "$DIR/solver.py" "$@"
  fi
done

echo "run: no python3 interpreter found" >&2
exit 1
SHEOF
